hypotheses.paper: T-abs-one-way-membrane's ≤, and ≪_U by the timelike curves in U that respect the membrane, so that only left ≪ left, left ≪ membrane, left ≪ right, membrane ≪ right and right ≪ right occur (title, roadmap.toml:926); I±_U open, transitive, inside ≤ (evidence, :935)
hypotheses.note: ≤ is oneWayMembrane's, the same relation (chronalMembrane_le, Iff.rfl, :194). ≪_U := TransGen (chronalMembraneStep U) (:94, :163): a step a → b is a.1 < b.1 ∧ a.2 < b.2 (strictly future timelike in null coordinates), segment ℝ a b ⊆ U, and a.2 ≤ a.1 → b ∈ membraneRight (from R̄ = {x¹ ≥ 0} only into R = {x¹ > 0}). Every field of Causality is discharged: lt_trans by TransGen.trans, lt_mono by inclusion, le_of_lt step by step (chronalMembraneStep.membraneStep, :101), isOpen_lt_right/left by moving the end of the last step / the start of the first (chronalMembraneStep.eventually_right :125, eventually_left :141; the segment by eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen :108, a thickening of the compact segment). At U = M the closed form x ≪ y ⟺ x <_Mink y ∧ (x ∈ R̄ → y ∈ R) (chronalMembrane_lt_top_iff, :204) is exactly the evidence's I±(m), I⁻(p), I⁺(r) and full cones otherwise. The planner's claim that the full one-way Minkowski chronology fails openness is proved: not_exists_causality_naive_membrane_chronology (:245), I⁻((0, 1)) contains (−1/2, −1/2) and none of its right neighbours (not_isOpen_naive_membrane_Iminus, :225)

questions: '≪_U by the timelike curves in U that respect the membrane' (roadmap.toml:926): the Lean takes polygonal chains of future timelike segments in U, and reads 'respect the membrane' as: once the curve meets R̄ = {x¹ ≥ 0} at a parameter, it lies in R at every later parameter (which along the curve allows exactly the title's five pairs). For a chain this is the per-step side condition, since x¹ is affine along a segment (pos_affine_of_nonneg, :296). The two definitions give the same ≪_U (inscribe a polygon in a timelike curve in U: its edges are timelike and in U, the side condition holds at the vertices), argued and not formalised, since no Minkowski model may be imported in layer 1. This is the reading taken. The witness is the polygonal causality, and its own chronal curves realise every ≪_U (chronalMembrane_causallyArcConnected).

hypotheses.paper: chronal neighbours: I±_U non-empty in every open set (evidence)
hypotheses.note: Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours (ladder.toml:346). In a ball of radius ρ about v inside V, v − (ρ/2, ρ/4) ≪_V v ≪_V v + (ρ/2, ρ/4), by one segment each (:263). The tilt to the right keeps the side condition at the membrane: v − (ρ/2, ρ/4) ∈ R̄ forces v ∈ R, and v ∈ R̄ forces v + (ρ/2, ρ/4) ∈ R. With the planner's untilted diagonal v − (ε, ε) the past step from a membrane point would fail the side condition

hypotheses.paper: causally arc-connected for both relations, hence absolutely minimal, on every open set too if cheap (the delicate step: every ≪_U realised by a chronal curve in U, ArcConnected.lean:127-131)
hypotheses.note: Causal.Causality.CausallyArcConnected (ladder.toml:274). The ≤ half by the one-way membrane's causal curves (the same ≤, defeq). The ≪ half: a chronal step is realised by its affine parametrisation, a ChronalCurveOn of the new causality (chronalMembraneStep.chronalCurveOn, :320): near each parameter a sub-segment stays in a ball inside the given open N, convex, its ends are strictly ordered, and the side condition passes to sub-segments (pos_affine_of_nonneg, :296: if 0 ≤ d_a → 0 < d_b then along the affine x¹ a non-negative value is followed only by positive ones). A chain by CurveOn.exists_concat (:349). The delicate step holds. Absolutely minimal by CausallyArcConnected.absolutelyMinimal (:371), on every open set for every cover by CausallyArcConnectedOn.absolutelyMinimalOn (:376)
from chronal neighbours, Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours.tarentin (:384); oneWayMembrane_tarentin also applies by defeq (diamonds read ≤ only)

hypotheses.paper: causally open in the future and not in the past
hypotheses.note: J± read ≤ only, which is oneWayMembrane's: CausallyOpenFuture, ¬ dual.CausallyOpenFuture, an open set is causally open in the past iff it misses the membrane, ¬ CausallyOpen, ¬ LocallyCausallyOpen, each by defeq from Causal.OneWayMembrane (:389-412), as kb/0052 describes

hypotheses.paper: neither push-up nor locally push-up: r on the membrane, r ≤ v ≪ w with v, w left near r, r ≪ w excluded (evidence)
hypotheses.note: chronalMembrane_not_pushUpOn (:429): no open W containing a membrane point m has PushUpOn W. With a ball of radius r about m in W: m ≤_W (m.1, m.2 + r/2) ≪_W (m.1 + r/4, m.2 + 3r/4), a null segment into the open left side followed by a timelike one inside it, while m ∈ R̄ is followed by points of R only. Hence ¬ LocallyPushUp (:464). ¬ PushUp by causal_ladder read backwards (:458): push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open, and ¬ CausallyOpen. The other half of push-up, x ≪ y ≤ z ⇒ x ≪ z, holds at U = M (chronalMembrane_lt_le_top, :419); in a general U it is not settled (not needed)

hypotheses.paper: not causally plain (on a T1 space with absolute minimality, ¬ push-up gives ¬ causally plain)

readme_row: | `Causal.OneWayMembraneChronal` | — | ETT programme, layer 1 (T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal): the one-way membrane's `≤` with a chronology (`chronalMembrane`: `x ≪_U y` by chains of future timelike segments in `U`, each ending in `{x¹ > 0}` when it starts in `{x¹ ≥ 0}`; at `M` the planner's rule, `chronalMembrane_lt_top_iff`) is a library causality with chronal neighbours, causally arc-connected for both relations, absolutely minimal on every open set, tarentin, causally open in the future and not in the past, neither push-up (no open set meeting the membrane has it) nor locally push-up, not causally plain; its time reversal likewise, and not causally open in the future (`chronalMembrane_separates`, `chronalMembrane_dual_separates`); the full one-way Minkowski chronology is no causality's `≪` (`not_exists_causality_naive_membrane_chronology`); either reading of `defi:causalite`; 2026-11-21 |
kb_proposals: pattern — A chronology on a polygonal causality. Take ≪_U := TransGen of a strict step whose side condition is closed in the start and open in the end (here a ∈ R̄ → b ∈ R). Then isOpen_lt_right and isOpen_lt_left reduce to moving the end of the last step or the start of the first (chronalMembraneStep.eventually_right, .eventually_left). The segment stays in U by Causal.eventually_segment_subset_of_isOpen (a thickening of the compact segment). The condition a ∈ R → b ∈ R is open in neither end and gives no causality (Causal.not_exists_causality_naive_membrane_chronology). With ≤ shared, every ≤-only property transfers by `:= oneWayMembrane_…` (kb/0052) (T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal).

pattern — Chronal neighbours without push-up, in either reading: Causal.chronalMembrane is absolutely minimal on every open set, causally arc-connected, tarentin and causally open in the future, and neither locally push-up nor causally plain nor causally open. For the ladder: ¬ PushUp and ¬ CausallyPlain come from ¬ CausallyOpen by causal_ladder read backwards (push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open, absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up, T1). The time reversal's seven negations come from ¬ dual.CausallyOpenFuture alone. Chronal neighbours at a membrane point want a tilted pair v ∓ (2ε, ε), not v ∓ (ε, ε) (T-abs-one-way-membrane-chronal).

for_keeper.load_bearing: The dual's to = locally_causally_open_future settles all 7 chronal_neighbours pairs on its own. This uses the backward reading (T-tool-ladder-py-2): lacking it, the time-reversed membrane lacks causally_open_future, causally_open and locally_causally_open. Since it has chronal_neighbours, push_up ∧ chronal_neighbours ⇒ causally_open makes it lack push_up. Since it is absolutely minimal, absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up makes it lack causally_plain, and absolutely_minimal ∧ locally_push_up ⇒ push_up makes it lack locally_push_up. Read forwards only, the 7 entries settle the pairs one to one: the membrane's to = locally_causally_open settles → causally_open and → locally_causally_open; → locally_push_up settles → push_up and → locally_push_up; → causally_plain settles → causally_plain; the dual's to = locally_causally_open_future settles → causally_open_future and → locally_causally_open_future. to = causally_open and to = push_up (membrane) and to = causally_open_future (dual) are implied by the others and kept because the witnesses state them

notes: One new file, sorry-free and warningAsError-clean, namespace Causal. It graduates unchanged as Causal/OneWayMembraneChronal.lean (module Causal.OneWayMembraneChronal). It imports Causal.OneWayMembrane (reused, not copied: membraneStep, oneWayMembrane's ≤ verbatim, its causal curves, causal openness, the past-openness iff, the time function, non-compactness) and Causal.Ladder.Rules (causal_ladder, used four times in the main orientation and seven in the dual). Causal.HalfLitDual, RationalLineExtras and PushUpNotOpen already import Causal.Ladder.Rules from the strict library. If a future [[implies]] edge ever had its witness here, Rules would import this module and close a cycle; no edge does. membraneStep.shift and oneWayMembrane_Jminus_mem_nhds were not needed directly: the ≪-openness is a one-step argument, and every J± fact transfers by defeq from Causal.OneWayMembrane. Every argued fact of the evidence is confirmed and nothing is refuted. The delicate step (causal arc-connectedness of ≪) holds. The rule 'once in R̄, into R' satisfies every axiom of Causal/Causality.lean, and its naive variant 'once in R, stays in R' provably does not (not_exists_causality_naive_membrane_chronology), as the planner said. One detail differs from a naive reading of the sketch: chronal neighbours at a membrane point need a tilted pair v ∓ (2ε, ε); v − (ε, ε) stays on the membrane and is no chronal past of v. Beyond the target: the sharp local failure of push-up (every open set meeting the membrane), the first half of push-up at M, the closed form of ≪_M, the bare and existential forms. Open, not needed: push-up's first half in a general U, and push-up on open sets missing the membrane. The reading of 'timelike curves that respect the membrane' as polygonal chains with the per-step side condition is a question for the master (labels[0].questions), stated as the sibling's SCOPE states it for ≤. The scaffold root is not edited (kb/0025: the axiom sweep does not see the module until it graduates). No ledger, curation, register, roadmap, ladder, README or kb file was touched. Simulations and checks ran on copies in /tmp/owmc. The keeper's recording is a target the planner adds (the evidence: 'Its recording is a keeper target the planner adds when it closes').
